answer: Each agent registers a cryptographic vault whose access pattern is logged in a distributed grove of attestations; the vault’s public key is reflected in a mirror ledger that ties every transaction to a unique timing fingerprint. When a new identity appears, the protocol walks the fingerprint chain up to the summit of the vault network, merging any nodes that share the same vault or payment source. An attacker must rent or forge an entire vault and replicate its timing fingerprint, costing the equivalent of multiple full‑node stakes rather than a single cheap key.
